_comment_family: Courier Prime ships as a family - a Regular, a Bold and two italics -
all four carrying 'Courier Prime' as name ID 1, with the cut in the
subfamily. Only the Regular is in fonts/, so nothing in this app can
answer to the bare family in its place; the machine the app runs on
is another matter, and that is what settles the name.
This face is used as a HIGHLIGHT, against Special Elite (see
cas-mortels/channel.json). A picked word is the one word on the card
somebody is meant to read first, so a Bold handed back in the
Regular's place through a local() fallback would be the highlight
shouting where it was meant to speak clearly, and an italic would be
a third voice on a line that already has two. So the full name (name
ID 4) is what gets declared, the same way the two Telegraf packs and
raleway-regular declare theirs, and for the same reason: the name has
to mean one cut.
That is also what separates this pack from special-elite.json beside
it, which declares its bare family. Special Elite has exactly one cut
and nothing else can answer to its name. This family has four.
Weight 400, which is the file's own usWeightClass. Stated rather than
left to 'normal' so the pairing is written down: this is the
unemphatic cut of a face whose Bold exists, and a synthesised weight
on top of it would be the thing the family name above is guarding
against, arriving by the other route.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name. Both
name this one cut rather than the family, so a machine answering to
either is answering with a Regular. 'Courier Prime' on its own is
deliberately absent: it is the name the Bold and the two italics
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied.
'Courier Prime' second is the same typeface by its family name, for
the machine that has the family installed but not under the full name
above - raleway-regular's first fallback is the same move, and it is
as close as damage limitation gets: the caption loses the file and
keeps the typeface. Courier New behind it is the one typewriter face
every Windows has, and it is a metrically different design rather
than a version of this one - Courier Prime was drawn to fix exactly
what Courier New does at small sizes, so what survives is the idea
The generic is `monospace` rather than `serif`, because that is what
this face IS: every glyph in it advances 1228 units, and a
proportional substitute would re-break every line it was asked to
set. Impact and Arial Black are absent for the reason
american-typewriter-itc-pro-bold gives - they are heavy display
grotesques, and this is a light monospaced text face.
